newsitem.title: USA: Burnham buys four properties for $79 mln.
newsitem.headline: Burnham buys four properties for $79 mln.

text.p: Burnham Pacific Properties Inc said Monday it bought four retail properties in the San Francisco and Los Angeles metropolitan areas for approximately $79 million.
The four properties contain 870,458 square feet of leasable space and have a current weighted average occupancy of 91 percent, Burnham Pacific said.
Three of the properties were purchased as a portfolio from BRE Properties Inc, a San Francisco-ased real estate investment trust, it said.
Burnham Pacific is an equity real estate investment trust with offices in San Diego, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Portland.

The largest property in the portfolio is the Fremont Hub Shopping Center, a community shopping center in Fremont. A Montgomery Ward Co store located at the center is not included in the transaction, Burnham Pacific said.
Also included in the portfolio are Santa Fe Springs Plaza in Los Angeles County, and Central Shopping Center in Ventura County.
In addition, it said it also acquired the Crenshaw/Imperial Shopping Center in Inglewood, Los Angeles County.
Since December 31, Burnham Pacific has acquired 10 properties containing 1,646,315 square feet of leasable space for a total acquisition cost of $146.75 million, it said.
It said that the historical yield on these properties -- calculated by dividing 1996 net operating income by the acquisition cost -- is 10.11 percent.
